title: The agent can finish a task: parameter parity, unattended posture, one tool story

AC1.note: src/harness/tool/metaproject-operations.parity.test.ts: schema declares depth+ranked, both forwarded to the port, and depth-2 returns src/c.ts where depth-1 does not (real computeAffected over an a<-b<-c fixture)

AC2.note: Round 2: search_code takes flags validated against the CLI table, MINUS -e/--regexp which map to the pattern field instead (they would move operand meaning). Parity test excepts them explicitly and asserts the regexp capability is still reachable through pattern. Verified: reverting search_code to {pattern,path} fails the test.

AC3.note: SUPERSEDES the earlier note: also asserts an unattended launch never opens a provider/mode picker (resolveUnattendedSelection: flags, then saved config, then refuse) and that --unattended with --chat is refused.

AC4.note: unattended.test.ts compares decideUnattended against decide() directly: both deny, matchedRules hard-deny:shell; agent-unattended.test.ts shows the tool never runs with or without the flag

AC5.note: unattended.test.ts: unattended-untrusted shell=ask resolves to deny via headless-fail-closed; agent-unattended.test.ts asserts the tool never ran; ask_user host rejects

AC6.note: Round 2: the allowlist that backs this was accepting *, bash -c *, and keryx * — 14 of 16 known-bad commands were reachable. validateUnattendedPattern now requires a literal command word and refuses any wildcard after an execution wrapper. agent-unattended-sweep.test.ts runs all 24 reviewed commands with no allowlist AND under a plausible one, with a real runner and a real git fixture; the tree is intact afterwards. Reverting either the validator or the -e rejection fails the sweep.

AC7.note: agent-unattended.test.ts: with no flag an ask still prompts and a yes still executes; with no approver the refusal wording is byte-identical to before

AC8.note: SUPERSEDES the earlier note: the header claim is now a behavioural assertion on shellHeaderMeta() rather than a grep of source text; the TUI seam check remains, stated as the weaker guarantee it is.

AC9.note: agent-tool-surface.test.ts builds the real registered array via buildAgentTools and asserts the instruction and the shell help name exactly that set, in both directions

AC10.note: agent-tool-surface.test.ts asserts the shell-first sentence and the graph/health/memory/flow catch-all are gone and that the replacement routes tool-answerable questions to the tool

AC12.note: bun run check: 3173 pass, 14 skip (all pre-existing), 0 fail; bun run check:doc-links: 640 links, 0 broken. Includes the merged flow-3 base.

AC13.note: Round 2: removed the "first token does not constrain" claim (falsified) and narrowed the credential claim to keryx auth.json/permissions.json, stating plainly that an exact allowlisted cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa runs. Run-record format corrected to include +allow(N). Added the harness run --tools paragraph.
